On load, `AuthLoader` in `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the app and calls `useUser` from `src/lib/auth.tsx`, which runs `getUser`, a GET to `/auth/me`. While that request is pending, the loader shows a spinner. If it succeeds, `user.data` holds the user. If it fails, `user.data` stays empty. `ProtectedRoute` in `src/lib/auth.tsx` wraps the `/app` routes (set up in `src/app/router.tsx`). When `user.data` is empty it renders a `<Navigate>` to `/auth/login` with the current path as `redirectTo`. `AuthLayout` in `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx` handles the reverse case: if a user is already signed in and lands on login or register, it navigates to `redirectTo` or the dashboard.

Every request goes through the Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. Its request interceptor sets `withCredentials = true` so the session cookie is sent, and its response interceptor unwraps `response.data`. On any error, the response interceptor first shows an error toast with the server's message, or the Axios message if the server sent none. If the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to the login path, and then rejects the promise so the caller also sees the error.

There is a bug in the redirect part. The code does `new URLSearchParams()` (an empty object) and then reads `redirectTo` from it, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. Any query string on the page is lost, and a user sent to sign-in from a page with parameters will not return to exactly that page. The fix would be to read `window.location.search`. Also, because the 401 handler runs for `/auth/me` too, a signed-out visit to `/app` can produce both the `ProtectedRoute` redirect and the interceptor's full-page redirect, plus an error toast. I did not run the app to confirm that sequence, so it is from reading the code. I did not change any files.
